tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — SHORT RACEMES ON SEPARATE UPPER BRANCHES
tiles.details:
Flora field cue (Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, p. 1316) — Follow a leafy flowering branch all the way to its tip. It ends in a narrow, spike-like raceme. The regional Flora describes racemes 2.5–5 cm long.

The strongest field distinction from introduced KR bluestem is flowering architecture: little bluestem has many short flowering units dispersed among upper leafy branches; KR usually concentrates several longer fingerlike racemes at one terminal region. Inspect the true origin of each unit, not several overlapping grass stems. Color changes seasonally and does not certify identity. Existing source-labelled Texas images show actual short racemes but no connected Hays root-to-floret voucher.
tiles.short: Native little bluestem: trace ONE flowering stem to multiple short silky racemes, each at the end of a separate upper branch.
tiles.status: REAL SOURCE FIELD PANELS — SAME-PLANT VOUCHER STILL NEEDED

tiles.heading: 02 · PERENNIAL CROWN, KEELED SHEATH AND TRUE LIGULE
tiles.details:
Flora field cue (Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, p. 1316) — Look inside the blade–sheath junction for a firm membrane. The regional Flora gives 1–3 mm for the ligule. That range is specific to this reference; the existing Hays notes below cite a different treatment.

Follow flowering culms into the basal crown. FNA allows cespitose OR rhizomatous forms; do not claim all plants have an isolated non-rhizomatous bunch. Sheaths can be rounded or keeled and smooth or hairy. Part an actual leaf sheath at its INNER blade junction: the 0.5–2 mm ligule is a small membranous edge, sometimes fringed; conspicuous hairs outside the collar or along the sheath are NOT the free ligule tip. The Harms SCSC-L and USGS images show real sheath/collar areas, but the unfolded free tip remains unmeasured.
tiles.short: Tufted or short-rhizomatous perennial; true membranous ligule ~0.5–2 mm (FNA), distinct from long sheath-edge hairs.
tiles.status: REAL COLLAR PHOTOS — FREE LIGULE TIP WITH 1-MM SCALE NEEDED

tiles.heading: 03 · ATTACHED SESSILE / PEDICELLATE SPIKELET PAIR
tiles.details:
Flora field cue (Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, p. 1316) — Trace the attachments of one pair. The regional Flora describes the directly attached spikelet as 6–8 mm long, with a shorter, narrower stalked companion. Compare the attachment points before estimating size.

On a single mature hairy raceme, find the sessile spikelet attached directly to the axis and its companion on a short pedicel. FNA gives pedicels ~3–7.5 mm, rachis internodes ~3–7 mm, and pedicellate units that may be sterile OR staminate, with or without a short awn. Do not teach that every companion is a tiny fixed sterile nub. Existing Harms and Matt Lavin closeups document paired structures but do not establish one measured attached pair and a dissection from the same vouchered plant.
tiles.short: Sessile fertile spikelets ~3–11 mm; companion pedicellate spikelets ~0.7–10 mm across FNA's variable species concept.
tiles.status: REAL PAIR PHOTO — SAME-UNIT SCALE AND DISSECTION MISSING

tiles.heading: 04 · GLUMES / LEMMA / BENT AWN MEASUREMENTS
tiles.details: Each sessile fertile spikelet has TWO glumes enclosing florets; separate first and second glumes before measuring. WFO's historical broad treatment describes glumes ~5–10 mm, while FNA emphasizes the species' variation (sessile spikelets ~3–11 mm). The upper fertile lemma bears a twisted/bent awn ~2.5–17 mm (FNA); reduced lower floret parts can be hidden. The detached Harms SCSC-9 figure shows real anatomical pieces but is not independently linked to the same mature attached unit in SCSC-s. Never infer an awn insertion, lower lemma or glume from gross seedhead pixels.
tiles.short: Sessile glumes ~5–10 mm in WFO's broad treatment; FNA fertile spikelet ~3–11 mm and upper-lemma awn ~2.5–17 mm.
tiles.status: PUBLISHED RANGES + SOURCE DISSECTION — ONE ATTACHED MEASURED UNIT NEEDED

tiles.heading: 05 · CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES / KR WARNING
tiles.details: KR bluestem (Bothriochloa ischaemum) usually presents several longer fingerlike racemes near a terminal center; little bluestem has short silky racemes along separate leafy upper branches. Big bluestem (Andropogon gerardii) has a few stout terminal racemes and commonly substantial pedicellate spikelets. Silver bluestem (Bothriochloa laguroides) has whitish flowering branches and can confuse distant views; cane bluestem (Bothriochloa barbinodis) has conspicuously bearded nodes. Node hair on KR can vary by taxonomic treatment, so a 'hairless node = KR' shortcut is unsafe. If immature or only vegetative, retain bluestem sp. pending flowering evidence.
tiles.short: Separate little bluestem from KR bluestem by branch origins and reproductive pairs, not red color or one node-hair rule.
tiles.status: FIELD COMPARISON READY — NO SINGLE-COLOR/HAIR IDENTIFICATION

tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE / EXACT TWO LANE HANDOFFS
tiles.details: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO (Grass Photo-Finish): Hays source-vouchered same-plant flowering crown through upper racemes; 1-mm-calibrated fully unfurled inner ligule showing true free membrane and ciliate edge separately from sheath hairs; ONE attached mature sessile/pedicellate pair with axis segment and ruler, then glume/sterile/fertile lemma and awn dissection of THAT same pair; matched KR and other bluestem architecture. NEEDS_SITE_QA (Public Learner Readiness): audit all 16 photo records and 16 teaching panels, rights-filter out two original unknown-license files and any review-held photo; retain Bob Harms Selected Monocots credited educational-only rights (NOT CC) and keep separate DigFlora source-link-only without new permission; pixel-check 23 existing markers, EXIF/GPS, comparison labels and mobile overlay. Do not call 100% FINISHED until specimen identity, exact anatomy, rights and live Pages QA pass.
tiles.short: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS: 16 existing image records and 16 teaching panels; critical matched root–ligule–spikelet evidence and site QA still needed.

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: LITTLE BLUESTEM (native): follow ONE entire flowering stem: many leafy upper branches each end in a separate short silky raceme, typically one short raceme per branch. KR bluestem (introduced) makes a compact cluster of longer fingerlike racemes at one terminal region. For plants with no seedheads, examine the truly KEELED/flattened leaf sheaths and the collar on an intact low tussock: do not confuse sheath-edge hairs with the true 0.5–2.5 mm membranous, often fringed LIGULE, or treat red color as identification proof. A physically archived spikelet-pair close-up is present; its reduced stalked partner varies across little-bluestem varieties. The new USGS sheath photo is a labelled, provisional first step toward a measured collar macro.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: Perennial warm-season grass forming distinct, relatively tight bunches.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Narrow blades; basal foliage and stems can develop reddish, copper, or mahogany tones late in the season.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Numerous upper lateral leafy branches each end in a SINGLE short raceme (often about 2.5–7.5 cm, length variable); the short plume arises individually from a small upper sheath. KR's longer narrow racemes attach together in a terminal panicle, usually clustered 3–8 in Texas A&M's treatment, but Williamson County local flora reports up to 17 in complex plants.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: At flowering, first trace RACEME ORIGINS: LITTLE has numerous short solitary racemes on separate leafy upper branches; KR has multiple long narrow racemes in one terminal head. At nonflowering stage LITTLE has a notably flattened/keeled sheath and often a well-defined persistent basal bunch; KR can spread from a flatter crown and develop stiff papilla-based blade hairs above its collar. KR can have hairy or smooth nodes depending on local material; node hairlessness is NOT proof. Matched mature spikelets and same-plant collars close the uncertain cases.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

intro: LITTLE BLUESTEM (native): follow ONE entire flowering stem: many leafy upper branches each end in a separate short silky raceme, typically one short raceme per branch. KR bluestem (introduced) makes a compact cluster of longer fingerlike racemes at one terminal region. For plants with no seedheads, examine the truly KEELED/flattened leaf sheaths and the collar on an intact low tussock: do not confuse sheath-edge hairs with the true 0.5–2.5 mm membranous, often fringed LIGULE, or treat red color as identification proof. A physically archived spikelet-pair close-up is present; its reduced stalked partner varies across little-bluestem varieties. The new USGS sheath photo is a labelled, provisional first step toward a measured collar macro.
memory_rule: LITTLE: MANY SEPARATE SHORT racemes on LEAFY upper side branches. KR: MULTIPLE LONG fingers connected to ONE terminal cluster.
safety_note: All nine new Texas photographs are genuine copyrighted Bob Harms originals licensed for credited scientific/educational use, NOT CC. Some have a true printed mm reference, but ligule membrane and sessile + pedicellate pair are NOT documented fully opened and measured on one individual source. Original restricted Jean H., Minnesota and Illinois files are excluded from public gallery; preserve their private metadata. Specific anatomy sources now found as externally linked PHOTO EVIDENCE only: Bob Harms DigFlora attached pair/dissection and copyrighted G D Bebeau split sheath. Their independent public reuse rights were NOT established; do not treat them as locally archived. Hays voucher Lyday 147 cited, not photographed. STRICT same-plant 100% gate remains open. DEEP AUDIT: published author-drawn 'L' in DigFlora KR indicates true ligule on a photographed metric composite but does NOT alone establish the fine free-edge length or ciliation. FNA, Kew and SDSU sources vary on 0.5–3mm and fringe. The original 4 DigFlora photo rights are NOT the Selected Monocots grant; source links/fingerprints only. Complete connected collection/arrow-scale test still HOLD. The four original DigFlora files were SHA256-verified as real JPEGs in reports/schizachyrium-digflora-four-source-verification-20261022.json; not copied to the public gallery because the exact DigFlora/KR rights are unresolved. Its field treatment is local North Hays, not evidence that all anatomy photos show the same botanical voucher. Lane 2 card validation removed out-of-bounds featured photo index 15 (existing images[] count 15).
field_rule: CREW READY: a distinctive narrow perennial bunch with many upper separate SHORT racemes, fuzzy mature paired spikelets and flattened keeled sheath. For specimen-level positive ID, verify ligule and pair and compare actual KR terminal branching.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
comparison_text: At flowering, first trace RACEME ORIGINS: LITTLE has numerous short solitary racemes on separate leafy upper branches; KR has multiple long narrow racemes in one terminal head. At nonflowering stage LITTLE has a notably flattened/keeled sheath and often a well-defined persistent basal bunch; KR can spread from a flatter crown and develop stiff papilla-based blade hairs above its collar. KR can have hairy or smooth nodes depending on local material; node hairlessness is NOT proof. Matched mature spikelets and same-plant collars close the uncertain cases.

morphology.habit: Perennial warm-season grass forming distinct, relatively tight bunches.
morphology.leaves: Narrow blades; basal foliage and stems can develop reddish, copper, or mahogany tones late in the season.
morphology.inflorescence: Numerous upper lateral leafy branches each end in a SINGLE short raceme (often about 2.5–7.5 cm, length variable); the short plume arises individually from a small upper sheath. KR's longer narrow racemes attach together in a terminal panicle, usually clustered 3–8 in Texas A&M's treatment, but Williamson County local flora reports up to 17 in complex plants.
morphology.spikelets: Paired spikelets occur along the raceme; the fertile sessile spikelet bears a twisted/bent awn. The sessile fertile member contains TWO florets (upper fertile, lower sterile) within g1/g2 glumes, with upper lemma bearing bent/twisted awn. The companion PEDICELLATE member can be sterile reduced or more developed/staminate; Harms's A/F/P labels refer to axis, fertile sessile, pedicelled mate, NOT three fertile spikelets. Author dissection labels g1/g2/l_f/l_s/p_s on separately arranged parts.

eco_habitat: Prairies, savannas, open limestone sites, roadsides, and restoration areas across the Edwards Plateau and Blackland Prairie.
